subject: Commercial channel check: AWS Marketplace appetite + procurement cadence
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <amorgan@cardinalhealth.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Commercial channel check: AWS Marketplace appetite + procurement cadence

Hi Alex / Sam —

Thanks again for taking time this morning to walk through Cardinal Health's intended usage and initial success criteria. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so finance/procurement can triage your preferred commercial route.

Call highlights (brief):
- Primary usage: inference for medication reconciliation workflows (steady-state ~50k tokens/day, spiky during batch imports).
- Compliance: SOC 2 + audit trail required; data residency preference: US.
- Stakeholders: you (app owner), procurement@cardinalhealth.com (procurement), and finance (billing).

Procurement paths we reviewed:
1) Purchase order (PO) charged to Cardinal Health corporate account (longest lead, common for enterprise).
2) Corporate card (fast, but may require per‑card limits approval).
3) AWS Marketplace: consolidated billing and single vendor procurement via AWS (can be public listing or private offer).

What you asked us to provide:
- Procurement pack (MSA highlights, SOW template, PO instructions, certificate of insurance).
- Short note on Marketplace options (private offer vs public listing) and estimated finance lead times for both paths.
- A scoped pilot proposal and an initial purchase number to use for internal approvals.

Deliverables we will send by EOD today:
- RWI_procurement_pack_20260210.pdf (procurement checklist + PO template)
- RWI_SLA_Security_Appendix.pdf (SOC 2, data handling, logging)
- proposal_cardinal_20260210.pdf (30-day pilot pricing + success metrics)

Next steps / asks for your team:
- Please confirm preferred procurement channel (PO vs card vs AWS Marketplace) and the procurement contact for PO routing.
- If PO: share the PO template your legal/procurement team uses so we can prefill to speed routing.
- If Marketplace: let us know if you need a private offer (preferred by many enterprise teams) or if a public listing is acceptable.

I'll follow up with a short HubSpot link to the deal and a DocuSign envelope for the pilot if you want to expedite signature.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15‑minute follow-up with procurement if that helps.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147
redwoodinference.com
From: Alex Morgan <amorgan@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cardinalhealth.com, Sam Lee <sam.lee@cardinalhealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:07:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Commercial channel check: AWS Marketplace appetite + procurement cadence

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the writeup and the very clear deliverables. A few clarifications from procurement's perspective: 

- Our standard is to use PO for anything over $50k annually. For an initial pilot under $10k, we can sometimes use corporate card or a small PO, depending on internal approvals.
- On AWS Marketplace: finance is open to marketplace purchases because it simplifies vendor onboarding, but legal often pushes for a private offer so they can include our procurement terms.
- Can you confirm whether private-offer marketplace purchases will still allow us the SOC 2 artifacts and an audit log export for compliance? That is non‑negotiable for us.

I'll loop in procurement@cardinalhealth.com to give a more concrete timeline — procurement generally needs 2–6 weeks for small POs, 6–10 weeks for larger POs with additional legal redlines.

Cc'ing our procurement lead so they can review the pack you mentioned.

Best,
Alex Morgan
Product Manager — Clinical AI
Cardinal Health

On Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 09:22 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Quick internal: Cardinal marketplace vs PO routing

Lauren / Priyom — read Alex's note. Quick internal alignment and recommended approach: 

1) Risk/Compliance: Confirmed — private offer on AWS Marketplace still gets the same SLA/SOC 2 artifacts; we provide the security appendix and will include a data access/audit export clause in the offer. Put RWI_SLA_Security_Appendix.pdf at the top of the pack for legal.

2) Commercial pathway recommendation: propose a two-step path to reduce friction:
   - Step A: 30‑day pilot via corporate card or small PO (<$10k) to get data in and validate latency/cost.
   - Step B: After pilot, move to a private-offer on AWS Marketplace or a standard PO depending on procurement preference. Private-offer is often faster than a full PO because it avoids a separate vendor onboarding cycle for Cardinal, and finance appreciates consolidated billing.

3) Docs to include with pilot packet: prefilled PO sample (if they share template), simplified SOW limited to pilot scope, and a one‑page security summary.

4) Timing: If they opt for card/pilot this week we can start within 7 business days. If they go PO, expect 2–8 weeks depending on redlines.

I'll draft a companion note for procurement that summarizes the private-offer mechanics and the billing flow. Recommend we offer to run a 15‑minute walkthrough for procurement next week.

Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
